title: Noodles or Rice? China's Staple Flips Halfway Across the Country | China Travel Expert
description:
Here's a food fact that surprises most travelers: China grows more wheat than any country on Earth — about 140 million tonnes a year — and it's also the world's #1 rice grower at roughly 207 million tonnes. So which one is actually the "Chinese" staple?

The answer depends on where you sit down to eat. Northern China runs on wheat — hand-pulled noodles, steamed buns, dumplings. Southern China runs on rice. Cross the old Qinling–Huaihe line that splits the country and the staple on the table simply flips. One country, two completely different plates.

🧭 Expert Tip: in the north, order noodles and buns like a local; in the south, rice and rice-noodles. Matching the region is half of eating well in China.

中国小麦产量世界第一（约1.4亿吨），大米也是世界第一（约2亿吨）。北方吃面，南方吃米——过了秦岭淮河线，主食就换了。面还是米，哪个才是真正的中国主食？
